# Exact reference-adapted Gibbs duality and constructive ascent

24 October 2026, root derivation. Finite dimensions; natural logs. The general Gibbs variational principle and relative-entropy data processing are standard. Historical originality of this particular packaging is NOT established.

Let N:A→B be a channel, keep an arbitrary fixed finite reference R, and let a>=1. For normalized faithful X_BR define

 G_X=a (N* tensor id)(log X)−(a−1) I_A tensor log X_R,
 Phi(X)=Tr exp G_X,
 F(rho)=S(rho_AR)−a S((N tensor id)rho)+(a−1) S(rho_R).

Then the exact identity is

 sup_X log Phi(X) = sup_rho F(rho).

The output space can be restricted to the support of N(I) if necessary. Boundary states are obtained by faithful approximation. No interchange of a minimum and maximum is used.

## Proof and explicit witness transfer

For omega=(N tensor id)rho and tau=rho_R=omega_R, Gibbs gives

 log Phi(X)=sup_rho [S(rho)+a Tr omega log X−(a−1)Tr tau log X_R].

The bracket is exactly

 F(rho)−a D(omega||X)+(a−1)D(tau||X_R).

By relative-entropy data processing it is at most F(rho)−D(omega||X). This proves one direction. For the other, put X=omega (or its faithful approximation): the two relative-entropies vanish. Thus an entropy upper bound is EQUIVALENT to the explicit exponential upper bound, despite the appearance of a specially chosen reference marginal.

This corrects the earlier statement in wh3_gibbs_trace_construction.md that the exponential candidate might be strictly stronger. For W3 and a=2, its constant is exp(−ln3)=1/3, so it is exactly the same squashing question, expressed in a different representation.

For any given X, the Gibbs maximizer Y=exp(G_X)/Phi(X) is an actual input state. It obeys

 F(Y)−log Phi(X)=a D((N tensor id)Y||X)−(a−1)D(Y_R||X_R)
                  >=D((N tensor id)Y||X).

Consequently a violating X gives a violating physical input Y with at least as large a violation. Conversely a violating rho gives X=N(rho) whose exponential objective is at least F(rho). This is a positive, same-channel witness transfer, not a formal nonpositive lift or an acquired experiment.

Set X_next=(N tensor id)Y. Applying the preceding inequality and the converse bound yields

 log Phi(X_next)−log Phi(X) >=D(X_next||X)>=0.

# A positive Gibbs-dual route to the antisymmetric entropy frontier

24 October 2026, root construction. The central inequality below is UNPROVED.

Let W3(A)=(Tr(A)I−A^T)/2. The uniform antisymmetric-qutrit squashing bound is equivalent, by the Weyl-flag argument in su3_phase_cycle_and_entropy_target.md, to

 2 S((W3 tensor id)rho) >= S(rho)+S(rho_R)+ln3

for arbitrary finite references and input states. This is NOT the stronger arbitrary-marginal mutual-information half-contraction statement.

A sufficient explicit noncommutative Maclaurin inequality is, for every positive X on C3 tensor R,

 Tr exp[I3 tensor (Tr_A log X−log X_R)−(log X)^(T_A)] <= Tr(X)/3.  (G)

Sufficiency needs no minimax interchange. Set X=(W3 tensor id)rho, so X_R=rho_R, and G=2(W3* tensor id)(log X)−I tensor log X_R. The Gibbs variational inequality gives

 S(rho)−2S(X)+S(X_R) <= log Tr exp(G).

For normalized X, (G) bounds the right side by −ln3. Faithful approximation handles boundary states if the universal inequality is established.

Physical representation: use the antisymmetric Stinespring isometry from C3 into wedge² C3. The matrix G is exactly the restriction to wedge² C3 tensor R of

 K=log X_BR+log X_ER−I_BE tensor log X_R.

K commutes with Swap_BE. Thus (G) is equivalent to Tr[P_- exp(K)]<=Tr X/3. Ordinary three-matrix Golden–Thompson/strong-subadditivity bounds Tr exp(K)<=Tr X, but this alone does not establish the sharper antisymmetric-sector weight.

For product X=A tensor C the proposed inequality reduces to the ordinary elementary-symmetric inequality e2(A)<=[Tr A]^2/3. It also holds blockwise for classical reference X. Neither proves the noncommuting-reference case.

## A tempting shortcut fails exactly

It would suffice to combine the ordinary full-trace bound with Tr[Swap_BE exp K]>=Tr[exp K]/3. This reflection-positivity guess is FALSE.

Take R=C3 and X=exp(−t Swap_BR), t>0. Write s=e^t+2e^(−t), so X_R=s I. In the three-qutrit permutation decomposition, the fully symmetric subspace has dimension10, the fully antisymmetric subspace dimension1, and the mixed representation has multiplicity8. Consequently

 Tr exp K=[10e^(−2t)+e^(2t)+8e^(−t)+8e^t]/s,
 Tr[P_- exp K]=[e^(2t)+8e^(−t)]/s.

The normalized swap expectation tends to −1 as t grows, the opposite of the proposed lower bound. But (G) itself STILL HOLDS: Tr X/3=s and its slack is

 s−Tr[P_- exp K] = 4(1−e^(−t))²/s

statement: For a finite-dimensional channel N, a fixed arbitrary finite reference R, and a >= 1, the reference-adapted Gibbs functional has the exact variational identity sup_X log Phi(X) = sup_rho F(rho). For each faithful X, the Gibbs state Y = exp(G_X)/Phi(X) is a positive input witness, and a violation transfers between the entropy and exponential formulations without a min-max swap. The alternating update X -> N(Y) is monotone under the stated premises.
